problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $g(x,y)=\frac{y}{3x-y}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{y}).$

feedback.problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y)=\frac{x+3y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2y}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x,y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
f(tx,ty)={t}^{n}f(x,y).
$$

So first, we compute $f(tx,ty),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}f(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(tx,ty) & =\frac{tx+3ty}{(tx)^{2}(ty)^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{tx}{2ty}) \\  & =\frac{t(x+3y)}{{t}^{4}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2y}) \\  & =\frac{t}{{t}^{4}}\cdot \frac{x+3y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}\cdot \frac{x+3y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2y}) \\  & ={t}^{-3}\cdot \frac{x+3y}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2y}) \\  & ={t}^{-3}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
f(tx,ty)={t}^{-3}f(x,y)
$$

and so the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y)$ is $-3.$
